item.title: Penicuik v Clyde in Scottish Cup postponed
item.description: [SNS] Friday's Scottish Cup tie between Penicuik Athletic and Clyde has been postponed because of heavy rain. The match at Montgomery Park has been rearranged for Tuesday, 27 October at 19:30 GMT. There are 19 more second-round ties scheduled for Saturday. Organisers the Scottish FA have released a list of potential rearranged dates should this weekend's wet and windy weather cause further call-offs. Also on Saturday, there are 14 SPFL fixtures, with two Premiership games scheduled for Sunday. Scotland to be hit with 80mph wind gusts as Storm Boelo alert upgraded to amber Two storms in two days as Austen and Boelo target UK Latest BBC Weather Latest UK weather warnings

item.title: The other WWE couple who made it to Big E’s wedding
item.description: The other WWE couple who made it to Big E’s wedding appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Over a year after their engagement, Big E and Kris Yim—the sister of Mia Yim/Michin—have gotten married, and fellow WWE couple Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch made it to the wedding. A video has surfaced from the nuptials . Rollins and Lynch can be spotted wearing matching green outfits to the ceremony. The “Visionary” was in a green suit while his wife wore a green dress. Rollins and Lynch began dating in January 2019, and their daughter was born in December 2020. They got married the following year on June 29, 2021. They are one of the top couples in WWE. In 2025, they feuded with CM Punk and AJ Lee, another professional wrestling couple. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch at Big E's wedding 🥰🥰 pic.twitter.com/Nvhqewp0Xf — Wrestle_The_One (@Wrestlish_WAR) October 23, 2026 Big E and Yim’s wedding comes after they got engaged in May 2025. Yim’s sister is currently on Friday Night SmackDown and part of Jade Cargill’s Takeover stable alongside B-Fab. Michin is a former TNA Knockouts Champion, but she has yet to win championship gold on the main roster. Maybe her time will come soon as part of the Takeover. Meanwhile, Big E is a retired professional wrestler. He was forced to retire following a scary neck injury suffered in March 2022. During a tag team match against Ridge Holland and Sheamus, the former delivered an overhead belly-to-belly suplex to Big E. However, he landed on his head, and he suffered a broken neck and fractures to his C1 and C6 vertebrae. He started a career as an analyst and panelist for WWE. He made a return to TV during the Dec. 2, 2024, edition of Monday Night RAW for the 10th anniversary celebration of The New Day. However, Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods turned heel and kicked him out of the group. In October 2025, Big E formally announced his retirement from in-ring competition. Don’t expect him to return to the ring anytime soon. Related: 51-year-old WWE legend may follow in John Cena, AJ Styles’ footsteps by retiring soon Related: Drew McIntyre hilariously teases WWE return as popular masked wrestler

item.title: Liberali a doubt for Como vs Sassuolo as reason for Man Utd omission emerges
item.description: Liberali a doubt for Como vs Sassuolo as reason for Man Utd omission emerges Mattia Liberali is unlikely to be available for Como’s home game against Sassuolo on Saturday as the Italian talent is dealing with a muscle problem. Como may have to do without Liberali in their next Serie A match against Sassuolo. Why Liberali didn’t play a single minute vs. Man United FLORENCE, ITALY – OCTOBER 18: Mattia Liberali of Como 1907 celebrates after scoring a goal during the Serie A match between ACF Fiorentina and Como 1907 at Stadio Artemio Franchi on October 18, 2026 in Florence, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Gazzetta reports that the Italian talent felt muscle discomfort while warming up during Como’s 4-1 win over Manchester United in the Champions League on Tuesday, so he was not introduced as a substitute, as a precaution. According to Gazzetta, the former Milan and Catanzaro talent is set to undergo medical tests today, but he is highly unlikely to be included in Como’s squad for their clash against Sassuolo. LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – AUGUST 16: Mattia Liberali of Como Calcio runs with the ball during the pre-season friendly match between Liverpool FC and Como Calcio at Anfield on August 16, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images) Liberali opened his Serie A account last week in Como’s 3-1 away win over Fiorentina, scoring in his first start for the club. Como are already short of attacking options, with both Moise Kean and Assane Diao injured. The Azzurri sit fifth in the Serie A table with 14 points: four wins, two draws and one loss.

item.title: Tottenham loanee Moore urged to deliver as Köln boss Wagner steps in
item.description: Tottenham loanee Moore urged to deliver as Köln boss Wagner steps in While Mikey Moore has shown glimpses of his potential since joining 1. FC Köln on loan from Tottenham in the summer, he is yet to fully find his feet and is still waiting for his first goal involvement. Most recently, the highly-rated 19-year-old made only a late cameo off the bench in Köln’s 1-0 defeat to Eintracht Frankfurt last week. Köln still have high hopes for the teenager and are keen to help him develop into a player capable of earning an important role at Tottenham and in the Premier League in the future. “For Mikey, the priority now must be to continue developing as a player here and perform in a way that allows him to play an important role at Tottenham next year,” sporting managing director Thomas Kessler told Bild. Köln coach René Wagner held a one-on-one meeting with Moore this week as the club hopes to see him break his goalscoring duck against Schalke on Saturday. “He’s eagerly waiting for that one moment when it all clicks and he finally finds the net,” Wagner said, making clear how highly he rates Moore. “He can beat almost any opponent in the league in a one-on-one situation,” he added. Köln and Germany legend Pierre Littbarski is also hoping Moore will finally score his first goal for the club this weekend. “I hope Moore starts finding the net soon, too. He has good movement, a certain degree of pace and is willing to take risks. I hope he doesn’t get lost in the mediocrity. He’s had plenty of chances to score,” Littbarski told Bild.

item.title: WRU bosses under pressure to resign after £18m loss
item.description: WRU turnover rose but overall losses got worse for the latest financial year [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Welsh Rugby Union bosses are facing calls to resign following the announcement it suffered an £18m loss for the latest financial year. The WRU also warned it is forecasting a similar loss for next year with chief financial officer Gavin Marshall admitting the organisation "can't go on like this". Soaring operating costs, lower ticket sales and reduced fan spending have been blamed for the latest losses. The union said the figures prove running four professional clubs in Wales is unsustainable as it looks to cut the number of regions to three from 2028. Former Wales international Alex Cuthbert has criticised a "lack of leadership" from the WRU while Swansea council leader Rob Stewart accused the organisation of mismanagement. "I'm really clear on what needs to be done, the chief executive [Abi Tierney] and the board need to go. They've completely mismanaged the game in Wales," Stewart told Radio Wales Breakfast . "I'm not surprised by the financial situation. [We've got] half-empty stadiums at the national stadium, fans voting with their feet and we've seen some of our best players drift over the border into England. "[There has been] complete uncertainty in the game for over 18 months and the WRU is changing its plans on a quarterly basis, it appears. "All of those things contributed to the financial state and it is mismanagement, let's call it what it is. "What we need though is certainty. We've got enough quality players in Wales to sustain four sides. We've got enough income going into the WRU to sustain four sides. They just need to manage it better." Scrum V: Is Welsh rugby living beyond its means? Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls Can people fall back in love with Welsh rugby? Marshall admitted the £18m loss - compared to £7.2m the previous year - was hugely disappointing and that the WRU board "would take accountability". But former Wales wing Cuthbert told the Scrum V Podcast the figures raise wider questions about leadership and the long-term direction of the game. "They [WRU] is going to lose another £16m next year," said Cuthbert. "The lack of ticket sales coincides with probably losing 18 straight games and not having the most successful international team, but that is their role. "If a company was losing that much money over that period of time there would probably be quite a few changes. "What it shows is a lack of leadership and probably a lack of communication with the public as well. Big decisions have got to be made over the next couple of months." Cuthbert also questioned the way the WRU has handled plans to reduce the number of professional regions. Scrum V: Is Welsh rugby living beyond its means? Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls Can people fall back in love with Welsh rugby? Marshall admitted the £18m loss - compared to £7.2m the previous year - was hugely disappointing and that the WRU board "would take accountability". But former Wales wing Cuthbert told the Scrum V Podcast the figures raise wider questions about leadership and the long-term direction of the game. "They [WRU] is going to lose another £16m next year," said Cuthbert. "The lack of ticket sales coincides with probably losing 18 straight games and not having the most successful international team, but that is their role. St Helen's has undergone a £5m redevelopment [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Ospreys play at their newly renovated St Helen's for the first time on Saturday in a Welsh derby against Dragons. And Stewart has defended the council's decision to invest in the stadium, despite uncertainty over the Ospreys' long-term future beyond June 2028. "We did have to decide if we were going to allow the stadium to continue to deteriorate or are we going to invest in it," he said. "It's a fantastic community stadium and it's going to be used not just by the Ospreys but by [Swansea], university teams, by our community teams. "The whole model we've built around this stadium is something the WRU should look at for other locations around Wales. "It's a really sustainable way of delivering not only first class and elite rugby in Wales, but community rugby."

item.title: Fabian Hürzeler 'really focused' on Brighton job amid Man Utd links
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Brighton and Hove Albion manager Fabian Hurzeler gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Brighton and Hove Albion and Crystal Palace at the American Express Stadium. (is associated with: «Fabian Hürzeler 'really focused' on Brighton job amid Man Utd links») Gareth Fuller/PA Wire/dpa Brighton & Hove Albion head coach Fabian Hürzeler insists he remains fully focused on his own job and has the utmost respect for the work "great human being" Michael Carrick is doing at Manchester United. A humiliating 4-1 loss away to Como in the Champions League on Wednesday night and the criticism from captain Bruno Fernandes which followed has put further scrutiny on Carrick's position. Following the Seagulls' fine start to the new campaign, Hürzeler is one of the names touted as a possible replacement for Carrick at Old Trafford should the club decide to make another managerial change. The German coach, though, maintains he is only thinking about how to keep Brighton moving forward into this weekend's game at Liverpool, with his side held to a goalless draw in the Conference League away to Czech minnows Jablonec on Thursday night. "I am really focused on my job here," Hürzeler said at a press conference. "I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days. "Beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick, for what he has done with Manchester United at the end of last season. "He is a great human being, he is a great personality. Every time we meet each other, we have a really good relationship, so therefore I really respect him and there is nothing more to say about that." Despite drawing a blank against Jablonec, Brighton head into the weekend's fixtures as the Premier League's top scorers with 23 goals. Hürzeler remains determined to get more out of his squad. "I am really privileged to be in this situation here, and I always mention that I am part of a journey," he said. "I always emphasise as well that I still have this feeling when I go to bed that we are not finished with our journey, and I am not 100 per cent satisfied and happy with where we are. "There is still improvements we can do, still a lot of potential to get out of the players, and therefore I really want to work on that together with my players, together with my staff. "I have great experts around me. I have a great group of players who support me, who give everything for this club and we built this over the last years. "We had tough periods, we have good periods, but I think to build these kind of relationships, you need time, you need connections and you don't take these things for granted."

item.title: Goldin Is Expanding Its Franchise Playbook With the Los Angeles Rams
item.description: Following its Lakers announcement, Goldin’s latest agreement with the Rams expands its role in game-used memorabilia and team-operated auctions as the company develops relationships across professional sports. “We’re not looking to sign 100 teams.” That was Ken Goldin’s response when asked about his company’s plans to expand partnerships across professional sports leagues during an October interview with Sam Goodman, Mantel contributor and founder of SOMOS Index, at the launch of Goldin’s multiyear partnership with the Los Angeles Lakers. Goldin Is Bringing Lakers History Closer to the Game Instead, the auction house’s founder described a selective approach focused on organizations with strong fan communities, established traditions and championship potential. On October 22, Goldin announced another agreement reflecting that strategy, naming the eBay-owned company the Official Auction House Partner of the Los Angeles Rams. The multiyear partnership will provide collectors with access to select game-worn jerseys, game footballs and memorabilia from the team’s sidelines and locker rooms. Items will be made available through Goldin’s auctions and eBay Live programming during the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. “The Rams are a storied franchise with a rich history,” Goldin said in the announcement. “We’re excited to bring memorabilia from their electric on-field moments directly to fans in Los Angeles and around the world through dedicated auctions and our Goldin on eBay Live programming.” The agreement builds on an existing relationship between the two organizations. Goldin and the Rams previously announced a partnership in December 2021 involving game-used memorabilia and fan experiences. The latest agreement establishes Goldin’s official auction house designation while extending its role into the Rams’ digital auction operations. Beyond offering collectibles through its established marketplace, Goldin will provide the technology behind Rams Auctions powered by Goldin, available through TheRams.com and the team’s mobile app. The arrangement gives fans a team-branded destination for bidding on Rams memorabilia, supported by Goldin’s auction infrastructure. All proceeds from Rams Auctions sales will benefit the Los Angeles Rams Foundation and its community outreach programs. For the Rams, the agreement creates another opportunity to connect the organization with its supporters. “The Rams are committed to creating meaningful experiences for our fans, and partnering with Goldin creates a new way for them to connect with the team through authentic memorabilia from some of our most memorable moments,” said Jennifer Prince, chief commercial officer of the Los Angeles Rams. item.content:encoded: Following its Lakers announcement, Goldin’s latest agreement with the Rams expands its role in game-used memorabilia and team-operated auctions as the company develops relationships across professional sports. “We’re not looking to sign 100 teams.” That was Ken Goldin’s response when asked about his company’s plans to expand partnerships across professional sports leagues during an October interview with Sam Goodman, Mantel contributor and founder of SOMOS Index, at the launch of Goldin’s multiyear partnership with the Los Angeles Lakers. Goldin Is Bringing Lakers History Closer to the Game Instead, the auction house’s founder described a selective approach focused on organizations with strong fan communities, established traditions and championship potential. On October 22, Goldin announced another agreement reflecting that strategy, naming the eBay-owned company the Official Auction House Partner of the Los Angeles Rams. The multiyear partnership will provide collectors with access to select game-worn jerseys, game footballs and memorabilia from the team’s sidelines and locker rooms. Items will be made available through Goldin’s auctions and eBay Live programming during the remainder of the 2026 NFL season. “The Rams are a storied franchise with a rich history,” Goldin said in the announcement. “We’re excited to bring memorabilia from their electric on-field moments directly to fans in Los Angeles and around the world through dedicated auctions and our Goldin on eBay Live programming.” The agreement builds on an existing relationship between the two organizations. Goldin and the Rams previously announced a partnership in December 2021 involving game-used memorabilia and fan experiences. The latest agreement establishes Goldin’s official auction house designation while extending its role into the Rams’ digital auction operations. Beyond offering collectibles through its established marketplace, Goldin will provide the technology behind Rams Auctions powered by Goldin, available through TheRams.com and the team’s mobile app. The arrangement gives fans a team-branded destination for bidding on Rams memorabilia, supported by Goldin’s auction infrastructure. All proceeds from Rams Auctions sales will benefit the Los Angeles Rams Foundation and its community outreach programs. For the Rams, the agreement creates another opportunity to connect the organization with its supporters. “The Rams are committed to creating meaningful experiences for our fans, and partnering with Goldin creates a new way for them to connect with the team through authentic memorabilia from some of our most memorable moments,” said Jennifer Prince, chief commercial officer of the Los Angeles Rams. The announcement follows Goldin’s recent activation of its partnership with the Lakers, where the company outlined plans to source historical and contemporary game-used memorabilia directly through the franchise and introduce weekly auctions on eBay Live beginning October 28. That agreement brought together several elements of Goldin’s approach to professional sports partnerships: access to memorabilia through the teams themselves, opportunities to reach dedicated fan communities and recurring auctions supported by eBay’s live-commerce infrastructure. The Rams partnership follows a similar approach while giving Goldin an additional role as the technology provider behind the franchise’s own auction platform. Goldin has also announced a partnership with the Detroit Pistons, reflecting its interest in developing relationships across professional sports rather than concentrating on a single league. Each arrangement has its own structure, but the opportunity is similar. Professional sports organizations control valuable historical memorabilia and game-used equipment, alongside established communities of fans. Goldin provides the auction expertise and digital infrastructure to connect those objects with interested buyers. The commercial results will depend on the memorabilia offered, bidder participation and how effectively the franchises introduce their fans to collecting. For Goldin, the Rams agreement represents another development in a strategy that brings its auction business closer to the professional sports organizations producing the moments collectors want to preserve.

item.title: One Moment in Time: Distin's wonder goal at Villa Park
item.description: One Moment in Time: Distin's wonder goal at Villa Park Whatever happens on between City and Aston Villa on Saturday, we’re unlikely to see a goal similar to the one scored by our captain at the same ground almost 20 years ago. Men's Team Maresca says Haaland is 100% available for Villa trip In late November 2006, a very different period for both clubs, central defender Sylvain Distin scored a goal in our 3-1 win at Villa Park that was hard to believe. Distin was known for his extreme pace and a length of stride that meant he ate up ground without too much stress on his body. The Frenchman was the model of consistency at the back alongside Richard Dunne, with the pair a major reason behind City’s continued top-flight status during the middle of the noughties. Men's Team How can I watch Villa v City on TV around the globe? For all of his numerous strengths that made City very lucky to have Distin in our side, he was never a consistent goalscorer. This game landed midway through his fifth and final season with the Blues and he’d only managed four strikes in his first 177 outings as a City player. That’s why when the imposing No.15 tackled Villa midfielder Gavin McCann on the edge of our own box, no one would have expected what was to follow. He played the ball out wide to striker Georgios Samaras and most would have assumed that was the end of his role. Instead, Distin burst beyond the Villa midfield and demanded the one-two from Samaras. Two touches took him from the halfway line and into the box past the powerless Liam Ridgewell before a fine left-footed finish around goalkeeper Stuart Taylor. He got back to his feet with the huge roar of a man that was fired up and, somewhere deep down, had probably surprised himself. It was perhaps the most crystal clear example of the way Distin had led this side through example and sheer determination. City won 3-1 in one of our outstanding performances of a difficult campaign, eventually finishing 14th before a refresh under Sven-Goran Eriksson. As previously mentioned, that was Distin’s last term with City as he moved on for Portsmouth before spells at Everton and Bournemouth and retirement in 2016. He remains one of the best players never to be recognised with international honours by France. item.title: Texas vs. Ole Miss: How to watch, date, time, TV channel
item.description: Texas looks to end a two-game skid as Ole Miss visits Austin for the first time since 2013 and the teams meet for the first time as SEC opponents. (Ricardo B. Brazziell/Austin American-Statesman) In losing consecutive games against unranked opponents, Texas has hardly looked ready for prime time. But here the Longhorns are, back in prime time, as Ole Miss visits for a Saturday night SEC matchup. Texas (4-0, 1-2 SEC) is looking to right the ship after consecutive losses to Oklahoma and Florida. Ole Miss (5-1. 3-1), meanwhile, thumped No. 13 Missouri 31-3 last week. This year's game is the first between the teams as SEC opponents. Texas leads the all-time series 6-2, losing the most recent meeting 44-23 in 2013 in Austin. item.title: Josh McErlean to test 2027-spec M-Sport WRC car at ERC finale
item.description: Motorsport photo M-Sport is continuing the development of its 2027 World Rally Championship challenger at this weekend’s European Rally Championship finale in Portugal. The British squad will field an example of its newly developed Ford Fiesta Rally2 kit car at the ERC Rally Six Cities North of Portugal gravel event. The updated Rally2 car, featuring the FIA’s new update kit, broke cover last week courtesy of a week-long test on asphalt in Spain with the driving split between Matthew Wilson and M-Sport’s WRC2 driver Romet Jurgenson. View this post on Instagram A post shared by M-Sport Ltd. (@msportltd) Testing is set to continue this week with Josh McErlean taking over the wheel for an outing on Portuguese gravel stages, running as the ERC course car. The Irishman has been a regular in M-Sport-Ford’s WRC Rally1 programme driving a Ford Puma Rally1 car in the championship since 2025. However, McErlean’s future with the team beyond this year is yet to be determined. M-Sport is the first squad to commit to developing a kit to upgrade its Ford Fiesta Rally2 car to Rally1 status, with the team targeting a three-car line-up for the 2027 campaign. Earlier this year the FIA announced plans to introduce a concept that will allow Rally2 manufacturers to homologate an upgrade kit, costing €7,500, to offer “greater aerodynamic parity” between Rally2 cars and the all-new WRC27 vehicles that will form the WRC’s top Rally1 class next year. The WRC27 and Rally2 kit cars are built to two separate technical regulations and are expected to produce similar levels of performance. The kit includes new homologated front fenders, a front bumper and a rear aerodynamic device, while the car will also shed 10kg from the current minimum weight. It has also recently been confirmed that the car will run a 33mm turbo restrictor, which was ratified at this week’s FIA World Motor Sport Council meeting. Hyundai tests revised Rally2 car in Finland Hyundai has also been in action this week, developing its revised i20 N Rally2 car on gravel roads in Finland. WRC rally winners Kris Meeke and Hayden Paddon were joined by Adrien Fourmaux to put the car through its paces. Images of the car in action didn’t highlight any noticeable exterior changes. View this post on Instagram A post shared by 𝘼𝙙𝙧𝙞𝙚𝙣 𝙁𝙤𝙪𝙧𝙢𝙖𝙪𝙭 (@adrienfourmaux) Hyundai is yet to make any announcement regarding its plans for 2027. The squad has however been focused on developing its Rally2 car but has so far steered clear from committing to developing the FIA’s update kit to up-spec the car to Rally1 status for next year. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: 'I don’t play this game to prove anyone wrong': Sanju Samson after India's 1st T20I win over New Zealand
item.description: India wicketkeeper-batter Sanju Samson has stressed the importance of trusting his process and staying focused on his game despite the criticism and opinions that come with playing for the national team. His comments came after India chased down 230/6 with two balls remaining to record their highest-ever successful run chase in T20I cricket, beating New Zealand by four wickets in the opening match of the five-game series. Samson said he does not play to silence critics. Instead, he focuses on his preparation, keeps things simple and avoids letting social media reactions affect his mindset. “To be very honest, you can’t focus on what people on social media or others are saying. You have to stay committed to the process and create the right environment for yourself. Playing for Indian cricket is not easy, with so much noise and so many people having their own opinions. But I don’t play this game with the mindset of proving anyone wrong. I keep my cricket at the forefront, trust my process, respect my practice and focus on doing the best I can. I like to keep things simple and stay focused on what I can control, rather than letting outside opinions influence my mindset,” Samson told reporters after the match. Samson backs India's aggressive approach Samson played a key role in the chase, scoring 67 off 33 balls to give India a strong start. However, a middle-order collapse put the team under pressure before Naman Dhir struck an unbeaten 42 off just 15 deliveries to seal the victory. Samson credited India's attacking approach across the powerplay, middle overs and final overs for helping the team achieve the record chase. He said the team has continued to back this style of cricket since winning the 2024 T20 World Cup. “We approach the powerplay, middle overs and death overs very differently. Even when chasing 170, if we get off to a flying start, we make sure we try to finish the game in the powerplay itself. That’s something we’ve been doing really well over the last couple of years,” Samson said. He added that India must continue trusting their approach, even when it does not always produce the desired results. Samson said the team's priority is to build on what works, play to their strengths and put the team's interests first. India's four-wicket win gives them a 1-0 lead in the five-match series, with the second T20I next on the schedule. 135141193

item.title: MHSAA tennis finals: Lansing Catholic's Noah West wins state title
item.description: Noah West fell just short of his championship goals a year ago. The Lansing Catholic junior reached them this year. West improved from his runner-up showing from 2025, finishing as the Division 4 No. 1 singles champion on Thursday, Oct. 22 at the Midland Tennis Center. He defeated Goodrich’s Mateus Pimentel in the championship match 6-2, 6-2. West, the top seed, won each of his matches in straight sets while capturing the championship. Just 10 points were scored on him during the finals. He is the first No. 1 singles state champion for Lansing Catholic since Matt Heeder won the top flight in Division 4 in 2013. He is the fifth Lansing Catholic player to win a No. 1 singles state title since 2000, also joining Paul Heeder (Division 4 in 2010), Jordan O’Neill (Division 4 in 2005) and his uncle Kevin Borzenski (Division 3 in 2001). The championship ending for West helped Lansing Catholic finish tied for eighth with 13 points as a team. Lansing Catholic also had Jacob Payne make the semifinals as the No. 5 seed at No. 3 singles. This article originally appeared on Lansing State Journal: MHSAA tennis finals: Lansing Catholic's Noah West wins state title

item.title: Who is supporting Gianni Infantino and how many votes will secure re-election as Fifa president?
item.description: Gianni Infantino is facing a battle to cling onto his Fifa presidency heading into next year’s election after his botched bid to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors resulted in a significant loss in support. England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027 . But as the dust has settled on his privatisation ploy, Infantino’s bid for a third term has strengthened. His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf , the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”. Infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president . Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino: Who has formally withdrawn its support for Infantino? Uefa (55 members) 🇪🇺 Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian. The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”. More recently, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions. Concacaf (41 members) 🌎 Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject. After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.” Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief. England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 The English FA are one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027. Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding

England and Wales have been among the football associations to join European governing body Uefa in leading the charge for Infantino’s removal from power, formally withdrawing their endorsement of the Swiss-Italian for re-election in March 2027 . His allies have surfaced, with the likes of Mexico and Argentina joining Caf , the African football governing body, in reaffirming support for the under-fire president, and now the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) has reversed its position and backed Infantino with AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa underlining that there is “a true understanding between us”. Infantino needs 106 votes from the 211 member associations to be re-elected as president . Here is every country and confederation to have expressed their opposition or support for Infantino: Who has formally withdrawn its support for Infantino? Uefa (55 members) 🇪🇺 Uefa, the governing body for Europe, has staunchly opposed Infantino’s leadership. They threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions before Infantino’s eventual climbdown but has continued to assert that his position is untenable, even taking legal action against the Swiss-Italian. The body points to how there have not been “assurances” that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup “to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again”. More recently, Uefa general secretary Theodore Theodoridis has written to his Fifa counterpart Mattias Grafstrom setting out a series of questions on behalf of European members of the Fifa Council, demanding documents covering a series of Infantino controversies. Fifa has until 2 November to answer these questions. Concacaf (41 members) 🌎 Concacaf, the Confederation for North America and the Caribbean, came out in opposition of Infantino after being left stunned at the lack of consultation during the Fifa sell-off plan, which they went on to reject. After the plan was aborted, the confederation said: “This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative.” Concacaf president Victor Montagliani was initially seen as a front-runner to challenge Infantino in next March’s election but he now looks set to pursue another term as Concacaf chief. England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 The English FA are one of many European member associations to send a letter to Fifa withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election in 2027. Infantino’s apology letter that was sent around on Wednesday night changed nothing for the FA, who was “deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance” surrounding his sell-off scheme. FA chief executive Mark Bullingham (left) next to Gianni Infantino (PA) Wales 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁷󠁬󠁳󠁿 The Football Association of Wales were one of the first to send its letter withdrawing support for Infantino . “The ‌recent failures in good governance, processes, ‌leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgment ​have led us to a position ‌where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to ‌remain at the helm of world football,” a statement read. “Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.” Scotland 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿 The SFA’s chief executive Ian Maxwell told the BBC that the governing body’s position has “been clear” since Uefa’s collective statement. “We have aligned ourselves with the Uefa position and 55 nations are stronger than one voice. “Their statement since then has talked about a lack of confidence in the Fifa leadership and the Scottish FA agree completely with that decision. “The SFA will not be voting for Gianni Infantino come the re-election in early 2027.” Republic of Ireland 🇮🇪 The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) has followed in withdrawing its support for Infantino while backing Uefa’s stance. "Following an FAI board meeting, the decision was taken to rescind the letter of support that the Association supplied earlier this year," it confirmed. "It has since written to Fifa to explain its reasoning. The Association is grateful for the support that Fifa provides to Irish football, but recent events have raised significant concerns regarding governance, transparency and the lack of meaningful consultation.” Italy 🇮🇹 The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) took a few weeks to take official action but it has now withdrawn its support for Infantino's candidacy in the next Fifa presidential election scheduled. "This decision is intended to clearly and transparently express the FIGC's position - in full agreement with Uefa and its president Aleksander Ceferin - regarding the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning the governance and development of international competitions," FIGC said in a statement. Finland 🇫🇮 Finland kickstarted this process, with it being revealed that the Scandinavian member association was the first to send a letter officially withdrawing support for Infantino. Serbia 🇷🇸 The Football Association of Serbia then sent a similar letter to Fifa. “We would like to remind you that we provided our support to Mr Infantino in writing on 25 May of this year, but after carefully considering the events that have seriously damaged the image and reputation of both Fifa and its president in the past period, this is the only logical and rational course of action,” a statement read. Sweden 🇸🇪 Sweden’s federation (SvFF) followed suit: "At an extraordinary board meeting on Monday, SvFF has chosen not to support Fifa President Gianni Infantino ​in the upcoming re-election. "This is after a long-term assessment of the development within Fifa and the organization's leadership. The decision is based on recurring shortcomings in governance, transparency and management, which means that trust in Gianni Infantino's leadership no longer exists." Infantino has officially lost the endorsement of numerous Uefa nations (PA) Croatia 🇭🇷 As did the Croatian Football Federation (HNS): "The Croatian Football Federation has informed Fifa of its decision to withdraw the support previously expressed for Mr Gianni Infantino's candidature for another term as Fifa president. "This decision followed a thorough reassessment within the federation in light of recent developments surrounding the Fifa World Cup 2026 and discussions within our governing bodies. We consider our position to be clearly communicated to Fifa and have no further comment to add at this time." Albania 🇦🇱 The Albanian Football Federation also took the same stance, aligning with Uefa. “The Albanian Football Association has sent an official letter to Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafström, informing him that it has withdrawn its support for Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for another four-year term as Fifa President,” the statement confirmed. Greece 🇬🇷 The Greek Football Association has backed Uefa’s push for a change in Fifa’s leadership, similarly withdrawing support to underscore a united European front in opposition to Infantino. "The Greek FA (EPO) has taken a clear position against a candidacy of Gianni Infantino," EPO presdient Makis Gagatsis told reporters. "We saw things happen at the World Cup that are not acceptable to football public opinion. Then... came a programme to sell World Cup rights and we are clearly against it, so we withdrew our support of the Fifa president." item.title: Why Giants loved Dennard Wilson blasting their ‘embarrassing’ effort
item.description: Dennard Wilson didn’t name names. He didn’t need to. The Giants ’ first-year defensive coordinator on Thursday publicly blasted the effort of some of his players — two days after he did the same behind closed doors. item.content:encoded: Dennard Wilson didn’t name names. He didn’t need to. The Giants ’ first-year defensive coordinator on Thursday publicly blasted the effort of some of his players — two days after he did the same behind closed doors. Later Thursday, in the locker room, those players embraced the criticism, as they prepare for this weekend’s trip to Houston, where the Giants need their defense to carry them in quarterback J.J. McCarthy’s first start. They all know this: If they don’t fix the effort problems that emerged in last Sunday’s loss to the Saints, they won’t win the NFC East, even in a down year for the division. “I totally agree with him,” slot cornerback Dru Phillips said of Wilson’s criticism. “You watch some of that tape, and you’re like, ‘That’s bulls---.’ We know that we’re better. We took it to heart, as in: Let’s do it — and we’re going to be better at it.” Phillips was one of the players who loafed against the Saints. So Wilson’s words this week felt uncomfortable for him. That’s just fine with Phillips. “It’s supposed to be uncomfortable,” he said. “You’re supposed to feel that pressure. We all felt it, and it’s like: We better fix it. It’s an embarrassing moment when you’re not running to the ball in this game. You can’t do that.” Wilson didn’t like the downfield pursuit and tackling energy on a few plays against the Saints. The most notable was Alvin Kamara’s 31-yard catch-and-run touchdown that broke a 10-10 tie early in the third quarter. Jason Pinnock whiffed on the initial tackle, though he didn’t loaf. Several of his teammates clearly did — Jevon Holland, Tremaine Edmunds, Phillips and Jihad Ward (who has since been released). Holland is in the concussion protocol, so he is not permitted to speak with reporters. Edmunds and Phillips did address the play Thursday, after Wilson’s fiery press conference. Edmunds — who might be out a while with a shoulder injury — mostly dodged questions about his effort. Phillips did not. Phillips said he expected Pinnock to make the initial tackle, which he noted is “the wrong thing [to do] in football.” Phillips specifically said he did not run hard enough to the ball. On the sideline after the touchdown, the Giants’ defenders told each other: “Guys, we’ve got to hustle.” So they knew immediately that they had screwed up. “It’s embarrassing, because you have 10 other guys depending on you,” Phillips said of his lackluster effort. “When you’re not giving that hustle that you should be, you feel like: ‘I let everybody down.’ There’s no excuse for it. I’ve got to hustle.” Meanwhile, Edmunds — the Giants’ ninth-year middle linebacker — deflected a question about what he could have done differently on Kamara’s touchdown. “We’re not pointing the finger,” he said. “I’m pretty sure we all have some plays that we wish we had back.” Still, he said the Giants’ defensive players fully heard and understood Wilson’s message. “It’s not just his message,” Edmunds said. “It’s our message to each other: What do we want our defense to look like? Because at the end of the day, it’s our defense as players.” During Tuesday’s defensive meeting, Wilson spotlighted the plays he didn’t like from the Saints game — while directly (and apparently profanely) calling players out by name, including Phillips. None of the Giants’ players spoke in that meeting. They just listened to Wilson’s angry message and absorbed his critiques. When Wilson met with reporters Thursday, he vented about his players’ poor effort, putting his frustration out in the open — something his predecessor, the underperforming Shane Bowen, never really did. “Last week was one of our worst tackling games,” Wilson said. “I wasn’t happy with our effort running to the ball. We put some stuff on tape that was not characteristic of a New York Giant defense. It’s unacceptable, and it will be changed.” Wilson said he shows those lackluster plays and makes a point of calling out players directly — in both the defensive and full team meeting — for a reason. “We confront everything,” he said. “I look at guys that don’t run to the ball, and I call them traitors, because they’re traitors to the defense. When you have a traitor to the defense, you either have to make adjustments to get them off the field or they have to correct their behaviors. “Last week, we did not on every play run to the ball, and it was unacceptable. The guys know it. If your effort is bad, if you have a lack of toughness, it gets pointed out. When you have behaviors that are unacceptable, we’re not going to accept it. And if you don’t change the behaviors, we have to change the players.” The Giants’ defenders are not surprised by how directly Wilson has handled this situation. It is typical of his black-and-white coaching personality, as they noticed when he arrived with John Harbaugh in the spring. “Any time you try to be a dynamic defense, honesty is the best policy,” Edmunds said. Safety Tyler Nubin — who missed the Saints game with a neck injury — said players appreciate how Wilson takes things head-on, while striking an ideal balance between praise and criticism. “He’s going to shoot you straight,” Nubin told NJ.com. “He’s not going to sugarcoat anything. He’s going to tell you what you’re doing well, as well. He’s just real. That’s what you want out of a coach. “You want somebody to be honest with you. You don’t want somebody to be blowing smoke up your ass all the time. And you don’t want somebody motherf---ing you and only talking about the things that you did wrong. “There’s no gray area [with Wilson]. Sometimes, some coaches can give you a little gray area. Some coaches like to cover their own ass, but he doesn’t do that. He doesn’t really care about the outside noise.” Nubin acknowledged the obvious: Wilson’s approach is “definitely” a change from Bowen, who arrived in East Rutherford alongside Nubin in 2024. “I’d say he’s a lot more direct,” Nubin said of Wilson. “He’s not going to wait and pull you to the side. He’s going to tell you in front of the whole entire unit. Having that honesty with everybody, it just makes everybody want to play better for each other.” Last season, when Bowen was fired in November, it became obvious that his less-than-direct approach was the wrong one for these Giants. How will Wilson’s style play out over the long haul? For now, Pinnock — a sixth-year safety — said the Giants’ players left his meeting with resolve. “That was probably the best tough meeting to have,” he told NJ.com. “I’ve been in those type of situations where it’s just straight finger pointing [from the coach]. And you walk out, and everybody has their side remarks, like: ‘Ah, man, whatever.’ Nah, that was positive, and it was needed. It’s not like somebody feels targeted.” Pinnock said this stems from the tight relationships Wilson, 44, has built with his players. “It’s going to feel personal if I don’t know you,” Pinnock said. “Dennard, he talks to all of us on and off the field, jokes with us, learns our humor. He knows his personnel, so he knows how to get the best out of everybody. I think it was a good meeting.” So how does Pinnock think the Giants’ defense will respond in Houston? “How we should: Go get a W,” he said. item.title: WNBA All-Star tells Stephen A. Smith ‘people might be sleeping on’ key change Angel Reese made mid-season
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images Two-time WNBA All-Star Chiney Ogwumike has been speaking very highly of Angel Reese when appearing on First Take this week. Reese has had a fantastic WNBA Finals so far, helping her team take a 2-1 series lead into Game 4 this weekend. Despite the Finals still potentially having four more games to go, there is already talk that the Atlanta Dream star will be the MVP, with Ogwumike among those backing her to win the award. When speaking to ESPN, she said: “The ‘A’ in Atlanta right now stands for Angel Reese and through three games, she’s my Finals MVP. No question about it. What she’s been able to do has been truly impressive. “She’s averaging over 21 and 13 so far in the WNBA Finals. But more importantly, her team is 15-0 when she knocks down a three.” Ogwumike continued by telling Stephen A. Smith, who was part of the discussion on First Take, that ‘people might be sleeping on the fact’ Reese completely reconstructed her shot in the middle of the season. She said: “Stephen A. people might be sleeping on the fact that she completely reconstructed her shot thanks to Karl Smesko in the middle of the season and now when it matters most, she knocked down two of them things on top of getting steals, going coast-to-coast. “This is a 24-year-old young woman who might be on the precipice of winning, she already won Defensive Player of the Year, she could win a championship.” The Dream and the Golden State Valkyries play Game 4 on Saturday. Reese heads into the matchup having just become the first player in WNBA history to record a double-double in her first three Finals games. item.title: Real Madrid icon hails Lamine Yamal ahead of El Clasico: ‘One of the most important players in the world’
item.description: Real Madrid icon hails Lamine Yamal ahead of El Clasico: ‘One of the most important players in the world’ Barcelona will be branded as the undisputed favourites as they lock horns with Real Madrid this weekend, in the season’s first El Clasico . But while former players such as Gerard Pique are predicting an easy win for Barcelona , ex-Real Madrid star Guti has taken a different stance, predicting a win for his former team. At the same time, though, Guti has also acknowledge the sheer quality Barça have while also heaping praise on Lamine Yamal. Guti in awe of Lamine Yamal In an interview with SPORT , the former Real Madrid man was glowing in his assessment of Barcelona’s talisman, the chief threat his old club must contain at the Camp Nou. Guti has branded Yamal as a special player. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) “Lamine is very confident, right now he’s at a very good level, he’s one of Barça’s most decisive players and also one of the most important players in the world ,” he said. Despite his Madrid allegiances, Guti had no hesitation in tipping the teenager for the game’s biggest individual honours. “It’s clear that even though he’s from Barcelona and I’m not a big fan of that club, you have to recognise that he’s a fantastic player. “If he keeps playing like this, he’ll surely be a contender for Player of the Year and a Ballon d’Or winner in the coming years. He has a very promising future ,” he added. However, the former midfielder was quick to warn Real Madrid against focusing solely on the 19-year-old. “Real Madrid would be wrong to focus only on him, because alongside Lamine there is Fermin, who is doing very well; there is Rodri; there is Raphinha… Mourinho’s team has to look at all the players ,” he said. Guti also stressed that both sides boast strength in depth, even though Barcelona have been hit with multiple injuries in defence, with Jules Kounde now being ruled out for the clash . “Barça and Real Madrid are not just two or three big stars, they are teams that are all very good ,” he said. Guti’s prediction for the Clasico and Ballon d’Or Guti expects Real Madrid to win the Clasico. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) While he conceded the hosts carry a serious threat, Guti nailed his colours to the mast with a scoreline in Real Madrid’s favour. “I imagine a very entertaining match full of goals. I’d be very happy if Real Madrid wins, so I’ll predict they’ll win 4-2.” “But the truth is, I see the match as extremely tough for them, and that Barcelona has a big chance of securing the victory ,” he said. As far as the Ballon d’Or is concerned, Guti admitted he wants Kylian Mbappe to win but says the fight is open, with Yamal and Rodri also emerging as candidates. “I would love for Mbappe to win it, but anything can happen, I think it’s very open. item.title: Council agrees £500k boost for rugby league club
item.description: Featherstone Rovers went into administration in December [Getty Images] Wakefield Council has agreed to provide £500,000 to secure the future of professional rugby league in Featherstone. The financial boost comes after Featherstone Rovers went into administration in December and the club was denied membership of the Rugby Football League (RFL). The council's cabinet members voted in favour of a recommendation to release funds to support the RFL's plan to purchase the town's Post Office Road ground and lease it to a new operator. Lukasz Borcz, the council's portfolio holder for leisure and sport, told a meeting on Tuesday: "This model protects the assets for future generations and reduces the risk of further loss." It is hoped a successor club could be created and return to competition from 2027. Funding comes from the council's Rugby League Resilience Fund, which was established in 2021 to develop grassroots and professional rugby league across the district. The council expects the RFL to match the contribution, and discussions are also ongoing regarding further financial support from national funding bodies, the Local Democracy Service reports . Borcz added: "The benefits of taking this forward will include safeguarding a major community and sporting asset, protecting opportunities for participation and youth development." A report to cabinet members said talks had been ongoing about how a "phoenix club" could be established at the stadium. The document said: "Key to this is what happens to the future of the Featherstone Rovers assets, which are currently in the control of an appointed administrator. "It is proposed that the RFL acquire the stadium and associated land through the RFL Facilities Trust." They would then be leased back to the new licence holders of the club, the report said, adding: "The benefit of the asset being held by the RFL Facilities Trust is that it ensures that, should the club get into difficulty in the future, the assets are secured for future generations to ensure professional rugby league can continue in Featherstone." The council said funding would only be released once the RFL had demonstrated that a sustainable operating entity had been identified and had met "all relevant requirements". The RFL previously said it was grateful to the council for enabling the release of resilience funding and said it remained hopeful it could "find a solution to bring Featherstone Rovers RLFC back to the town". Listen to highlights from West Yorkshire on BBC Sounds , catch up with the latest episode of Look North . item.title: “He’s fine” – Andoni Iraola confirms massive Liverpool injury boost
item.description: “He’s fine” – Andoni Iraola confirms massive Liverpool injury boost Andoni Iraola Provides Bradley Barcola Update Ahead of Brighton Clash Liverpool are in a fine run of form at the moment, winning seven of their last nine games across all competitions. However, they face a serious test against Brighton on Sunday, who currently sit second in the Premier League table and have scored more goals than any other team in the competition so far. Andoni Iraola’s side will be without a number of key players this weekend with Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley, Jeremie Frimpong and Hugo Ekitike all already ruled out. However, speaking in his pre-match press conference, Iraola confirmed a massive boost for the Reds… Barcola Fit For Brighton There had been some concern over the fitness of Bradley Barcola in recent days, with the Frenchman training individually earlier this week. However, Iraola has passed him fit for the Brighton test, saying: “Yes, Bradley has trained today normally. He is fine. No problems. It was just a matter of dealing with the load and sometimes they have to stay inside.” “He is fine.” Photo: IMAGO Munoz Remains A Doubt Forward Victor Munoz missed the 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday and remains a doubt for this weekend. Iraola said: “He is dealing with some pain [since Brentford] and it was too early to play against Villarreal.” “I don’t know. I think it’s going to be difficult [to be fit for Brighton], but I really don’t know.”

item.title: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns gets major contract update from NBA insider with one guarantee
item.description: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns gets major contract update from NBA insider with one guarantee originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Knicks are going to be a team closely watched this season as they look to build on their success as NBA champions. The Knicks got everything clicking at the right time last season, and now it is up to them to keep that momentum going. The organization had the opportunity to extend Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart before the season started. However, the Knicks opted against doing so, instead focusing on the upcoming season. “As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of. As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season," a Knicks spokesperson told ESPN's Shams Charania. Before the Knicks shut down extension discussions, Towns reportedly wasn't satisfied with the offer on the table. Still, the veteran big man remains vocal about his desire to keep the core group together in New York. “I want us all to stay together. That's always been my main priority. Nowhere in my mind was a max contact was even thought about,” Towns told ESPN’s Malika Andrews. Of course, the question remains whether the two sides will ultimately reach an agreement. There are several important decisions for the Knicks to make, and team insider Ian Begley recently shared his thoughts on the situation. He believes there is enough common ground for both sides to get a deal done when negotiations resume. “An extension with Towns and the Knicks is going to get done - there's enough common ground there to figure it out,” Begley wrote. There is no doubt that Towns wants to stay in New York. At this point, it is simply a matter of what the Knicks are willing to offer him financially. New York has a strong core and will likely do everything it can to keep the group together. Although extension discussions are currently on hold, there is reason for optimism on both sides. The Knicks' future looks bright if they can maintain their core, and securing Towns' long-term future will be an important part of that plan. Nowhere in my mind was a max contact was even thought about,” Towns told ESPN’s Malika Andrews. Of course, the question remains whether the two sides will ultimately reach an agreement. There are several important decisions for the Knicks to make, and team insider Ian Begley recently shared his thoughts on the situation. He believes there is enough common ground for both sides to get a deal done when negotiations resume. “An extension with Towns and the Knicks is going to get done - there's enough common ground there to figure it out,” Begley wrote. There is no doubt that Towns wants to stay in New York. At this point, it is simply a matter of what the Knicks are willing to offer him financially. New York has a strong core and will likely do everything it can to keep the group together. Although extension discussions are currently on hold, there is reason for optimism on both sides. The Knicks' future looks bright if they can maintain their core, and securing Towns' long-term future will be an important part of that plan. item.title: Ligue 1 clash between PSG and Lyon postponed, running parallel to Ballon d’Or ceremony
item.description: Ligue 1 clash between PSG and Lyon postponed, running parallel to Ballon d’Or ceremony The match scheduled for this Sunday between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais, counting towards Matchday 8 of Ligue 1, has been postponed, the Professional Football League (LFP) has confirmed . At the request of the Paris Police Prefecture, which was concerned about the organisational arrangements for the event given that further large-scale demonstrations are expected in the French capital this weekend, the League, in agreement with the broadcaster, has agreed to reschedule the match to Monday 26 October – 24 hours later. As was the case last season, when Olympique de Marseille and PSG – who were due to play Le Classique on Sunday evening – ended up facing each other on Monday due to heavy rain, a French league match will therefore take place alongside the Ballon d’Or ceremony. However, several nominated Parisian players – such as Ousmane Dembélé (29), Kvicha Kvaratskhelia (25), Marquinhos (32) and Nuno Mendes (24) – will still be able to attend the event, having all been ruled out through injury. GFFN | Léo Aschi

item.title: Bompastor rules Chelsea star out for a few more weeks
item.description: Bompastor rules Chelsea star out for a few more weeks Sonia Bompastor has confirmed Naomi Girma is set to remain sidelined for several weeks with a calf injury, while Manaka Matsukubo could make her Chelsea Women debut against Crystal Palace on Sunday. Girma has been absent of late and Bompastor revealed the defender is still undergoing rehabilitation. “I didn’t have much information on Naomi before,” Bompastor said. “I gave the earlier information before the international break, but actually Naomi is now dealing with a calf injury. “I think it will take a few weeks for her to get back, so for now she’s just rehabbing. “She’s in a good place rehabbing and doing the things she has to do and to focus on. “We’ll see, but I don’t have any timeframe for now.” Stay up to date with all the latest women’s football news by joining our WhatsApp channel . There was more positive news on Matsukubo, with the summer signing potentially in contention to make her first Chelsea appearance against Palace. “I think otherwise I have the full squad available for the game on Sunday,” Bompastor added. “We had a few players who were involved in the Under-18 game and Manaka is also a player who could be in contention for the game on Sunday.” Chelsea captain Erin Cuthbert is also continuing to build up her fitness after returning from injury. The Scotland midfielder came off the bench in the 6-2 win over Tottenham and Bompastor says her workload will continue to be carefully managed. “Erin is our captain, she’s important on and off the pitch,” she said. “I think she brings a lot of energy. I think the quality she has as a player in and out of possession, it’s good news she’s back with us. “In this block we will have to build her up to be able to start a game and to perform for 90 minutes. “I think getting back to the team, playing 30 minutes in this league, is already a good step. “We have a plan for her all through this next block. “She’s performing at a good level and in training this morning she was again good. I think she will help the team to get good results and to perform.”

item.title: Hurzeler 'focused' on Brighton job despite Man Utd links
item.description: Fabian Hurzeler has distanced himself from links to the Manchester United manager's job (Glyn KIRK) Fabian Hurzeler said he is fully focused on maintaining Brighton's stunning start to the season and has too much respect for Michael Carrick to talk about speculation he could be the next Manchester United manager. Carrick's position as United boss is under threat after a seven-game winless run which hit a new low in a 4-1 thrashing to Champions League debutants Como on Wednesday. Brighton's free-scoring start to the Premier League season has seen Hurzeler touted as a possible successor should United make a mid-season managerial change for the third consecutive campaign. The Seagulls sit third in the table, behind only Manchester City and champions Arsenal, ahead of Sunday's trip to Liverpool. "I am really focused on my job here. I have no time to think about these rumours because we play every three days," said the 33-year-old German. "Beside that, I have a lot of respect for Michael Carrick, for what he has done with Manchester United at the end of last season. "He is a great human being, he is a great personality. Every time we meet each other, we have a really good relationship, so therefore I really respect him and there is nothing more to say about that." Brighton's scoring streak came to an end in a 0-0 draw at Czech side Jablonec in the Europa League on Thursday. Despite an excellent start to the campaign, that also includes coming from 2-0 down to beat United 3-2 at Old Trafford in the League Cup last month, Hurzeler believes his side can still improve. "There is still improvements we can do, still a lot of potential to get out of the players, and therefore I really want to work on that together with my players, together with my staff," he said. "I have great experts around me. I have a great group of players who support me, who give everything for this club and we built this over the last years. "We had tough periods, we have good periods, but I think to build these kind of relationships, you need time, you need connections and you don’t take these things for granted." kca/iwd

item.title: Steelers Reveal DeShon Elliott’s Status vs. Saints
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers strong safety DeShon Elliott during a game against the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 12, 2025. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Pittsburgh Steelers safety DeShon Elliott (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris. Elliott was a full participant at practice on Wednesday and Thursday. He was also an estimated full practice participant on Friday. The Steelers cancelled Friday’s practice in Paris due to rain and wind in the forecast. It appears Elliott is set to make his return to the lineup in Week 7 against the Saints. Elliott had his 21-day practice window opened and was a limited participant in practice on Thursday, Oct. 8. He was again a limited participant on Friday, Oct. 9, but was ruled out for a Week 5 return. Elliott was a limited participant in practice for the fifth straight session on Friday, Oct. 16 and was ruled out of a Week 6 return. Elliott has been sidelined since last October with a significant hamstring/knee injury that required surgery. He began to get back to action this preseason and played in the team’s second preseason game, but suffered a setback and started the season on the injured reserve list, pushing Jenkins and then rookie Robert Spears-Jennings to be forced in alongside starting free safety Jaquan Brisker. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said on Wednesday that is optimistic about Elliott being able to play this week. “I hope so,” he said before practice at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. “We have a practice plan for him. He’s doing really well. He’s chomping at the bit, so we’ll see how it goes this week. … We’ll see how today goes.” The Steelers released veteran backup Rayshawn Jenkins earlier in the week, signifying Elliott’s readiness to return. Alan Saunders contributed. Related Headlines Mike McCarthy Updates T.J. Watt’s Injury Status Steelers Injury Central: 2 Ruled Out, SJD on IR, T.J. Watt Limited Steelers Will Be Without Key Wide Receiver vs. Saints Read more at Steelers Now

item.title: Charley Hull catches attention with behind-the-scenes Sports Illustrated Swimsuit photos
item.description: Just over a week ago golfer Charley Hull lit up the internet with photos from a girls trip celebrating the upcoming wedding of fellow golfer Georgia Hall. “Final adventure before Mrs. Dunne status—mission accomplished. Love you my George —here’s to the next chapter with Paul. Good luck to him ffs 🤣 – only kidding he’s one lucky man,” she said in the caption of the post at the time. Hull is on hiatus from the golf course after most recently competed in the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship where she was in contention before a final round 70 saw her finish at 11-under and 10 shots off the lead. But her hiatus from the golf course doesn’t mean she’s not busy. MORE: Golfer Charley Hull stuns with new swimsuit photo on girls trip Charley Hull teases SI Swimsuit appearance Jun 6, 2026; Pacific Palisades, California, USA; Charley Hull hits her tee shot from the 10th tee during the third round of the U.S. Women’s Open golf tournament at Riviera Country Club. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) On Thursday morning Hull took to Instagram to tease a major announcement: she’ll be featured in the next Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue. “I did a thing…. @si_swimsuit ,” she said in the caption of the post which featured a few behind-the-scenes shots of the star golfer covered in a towel. The office Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Instagram account also featured Hull in a video from the shoot, which took place in Ibiza. Hull isn’t the only athlete in the shoot, either. Dallas Wings guard and former No. 1 overall pick Azzi Fudd also announced her appearance in the upcoming issue. While Hull isn’t competing this weekend, she’s entered to compete in the Maybank Championship next week in Malaysia. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Conte plays down 'unfounded' Man Utd speculation
item.description: Antonio Conte won the Premier League with Chelsea in 2017 [Getty Images] Antonio Conte has said he is not in "advanced negotiations" with any club in response to reports he has held talks with Manchester United. Italian newspaper La Repubblica claimed on Thursday that Conte had held talks with United's board about replacing Michael Carrick following the 4-1 defeat against Como on Wednesday. The report said the former Chelsea manager had demanded full control of United's transfer policy and stated his intention to appoint his own staff at Old Trafford. But, while BBC Sport understands Conte is keen on the job, the Italian says he is not in "advanced" talks with any club. "My name has been linked with numerous clubs, but there are currently no negotiations at an advanced stage," Conte wrote on Instagram. "I have read reports of financial demands and requests for full control that I have supposedly already made to the clubs mentioned, as well as reservations about what has been described as my "strong personality". These reports are unfounded. "Should a concrete opportunity arise, that will be the time to hold discussions with the club concerned and jointly consider the terms of a potential agreement, with due regard for both parties' needs and the qualities and approach that define my work as a manager." Carrick's future at Old Trafford is uncertain after a humiliating defeat to Cesc Fabregas' Como in the Champions League earlier this week. Although Carrick is set to remain in charge for Sunday's Premier League match against Bournemouth, sources have told BBC Sport that United have begun the process of identifying possible replacements. Former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe, Conte and ex-Germany manager Julian Nagelsmann are all understood to have their eyes on the job. Conte, who played for Juventus and Italy in a stellar career, is a free agent after leaving Napoli at the end of last season. He won the Serie A title during his first season in Naples, before a Supercoppa Italiana victory in his final campaign. The 57-year-old won the Premier League with Chelsea during his debut campaign at Stamford Bridge in 2016-17 and beat Manchester United in the FA Cup final the following season. He returned to the Premier League in 2021 when he replaced Jose Mourinho at Tottenham Hotspur. Conte's time in north London lasted just 16 months though, with the Italian leaving in March 2023 after criticising "selfish" players and the club's culture in a remarkable news conference. item.title: Pete Prisco tears into Saquon Barkley ahead of his return for the Eagles this weekend
item.description: Photo by Kyle Ross/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A return for Saquon Barkley is looking more and more likely ahead of the Philadelphia Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Dallas Cowboys. The running back suffered a hamstring injury during the Eagles’ game earlier in the month against the Los Angeles Rams. Barkley has missed the Eagles’ last two games a result but he has returned to practice. Now back on the field, Barkley spoke to the media and admitted that he pushed to play at the weekend against the Carolina Panthers. With so many important players missing for the Eagles, having Barkley back on the field will provide a sliver of hope ahead of the remaining weeks. However, Pete Prisco is not convinced that the 29-year-old’s return will actually make that much of a difference from what he has seen over the last 18 months from Barkley. Pete Prisco rips Saquon Barkley live on air ahead of Eagles return It has not been a great start to the 2026 season for Barkley who has managed 182 yards and no touchdowns through his opening four appearances. Despite showing his quality over the years, Prisco is not convinced Barkley is still all that. “He hasn’t been good since they won the Super Bowl. Let’s be real, he wasn’t good last year. A lot of it had to do with the offensive line. He also wasn’t very good. His offensive line that he has now isn’t very good either,” Prisco said on CBS. “Don’t expect him to step in there and just be Saquon Barkley, because it’s going to be tough sledding. Think about it: you’re facing a quarterback who doesn’t scare anybody, really. You’re facing an offensive line that has four guys on there that probably shouldn’t be. Some of them shouldn’t be starters. “I think you’d think he would help, but if the offensive line isn’t blocking now, the Cowboys aren’t great in the run game either. We saw Bucky Irving a couple weeks ago run wild on him.” The Eagles do need Barkley to pull a rabbit out of the hat, as they are now set to play the remainder of the season without quarterback Jalen Hurts. Whether he is able to return with a game-changing impact remains to be seen. It has certainly been a difficult season for the Eagles and Nick Sirianni will be looking to lean on the likes of Barkley in an attempt to end the year on a respectable note. The NFC East has been fairly poor so far, with top spot only one win away for Philadelphia. Read more: Malik Nabers sends clear message on Giants’ decision to start J.J. McCarthy Stephen A. item.title: “What the fans want” – Chelsea owners praised for listening to supporters – four years too late
item.description: “What the fans want” – Chelsea owners praised for listening to supporters – four years too late Chelsea finally changed their suicidal transfer policy this summer and have been reaping the rewards ever since. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Former Blue Gus Poyet has been speaking to Chelsea fans about their team and the changes made in transfer strategy this summer. Chelsea’s changed model brings instant results Danny Welbeck (Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images) “I think the approach has changed a little bit. I remember the first [few] years of the new owners, it was all young players and long-term, massive contracts, which, depending on the character, works or does not,” Poyet pointed out in quotes picked up by the Evening Standard. “I think now they are looking more for specifics. They would not have signed [Jordan] Henderson three or four years ago. That shows they have realised that investment was important, the future is important, but today [their strategy] is what the fans want. They do not want tomorrow. The fans want today. “You have got some young players, but you have also got experienced ones who have been around [for] a few years already. Now is a matter of consistency.” As we’ve said before, we’re delighted the owners have changed their model and that it looks to have been such an instantly effective change. We just wish they had listened to all the fans and pundits who were telling them from the day they arrived that this was the way go to. They could have saved a lot of money. In other news… Joao Pedro has been speaking about his relationship with Cole Palmer and how quickly it developed after his arrival.
