item.title: Bold predictions for 2026 World Series
item.description: The 2026 World Series is set to begin tonight, as the Milwaukee Brewers host the Tampa Bay Rays . Both franchises are searching for their first-ever championship. Milwaukee won a franchise-record 103 games, while Tampa Bay finished with 98 wins and reached the Fall Classic for the third time in franchise history. Here are four bold predictions for the series. MORE: 2026 World Series will be just second of its kind in past 100 years The home team wins every game Sep 27, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers starting pitcher Jacob Misiorowski (32) throws a pitch in the first inning against the St. Louis Cardinals at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images This World Series prediction has the Brewers winning all of their games at American Family Field and the Rays taking care of business at home. Milwaukee wins Games 1 and 2 before the series shifts to Tampa Bay, where the Rays win Games 3, 4, and 5. The Brewers then return home and win Games 6 and 7 to capture the championship. The Brewers enter the matchup with the better regular-season record and home-field advantage after winning 103 games. Tampa Bay won 98 games and enters the series after sweeping the Yankees and defeating Cleveland in six games in the ALCS. Junior Caminero hits three home runs Oct 3, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero (13) reacts in the eighth inning against the New York Yankees in game one of the ALDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Junior Caminero is one of the biggest stars in the World Series and could be in line for a huge performance against Milwaukee. The Rays slugger hit 42 home runs during the regular season, ranking among MLB’s elite power hitters. Caminero also finally broke through in the postseason during the ALCS, launching a clutch playoff homer in Tampa Bay’s series-clinching victory over Cleveland. The prediction is that the 23-year-old carries that momentum into the Fall Classic and hits three home runs against the Brewers. Christian Yelich hits .400 Sep 9, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich (22) rounds the bases after hitting a home run during the first inning against the Chicago Cubs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Christian Yelich could be one of Milwaukee’s most important offensive players throughout the series. Although he is no longer their star player, he is their captain and the team’s longest-tenured player. The veteran will step up when it matters most, and he should be in the starting lineup every game as the Rays feature a right-handed-heavy starting rotation. The prediction is that Yelich puts together an outstanding World Series, hitting .400 across the seven-game series and helping Milwaukee finish the job. The series goes seven games, with every game decided by two runs or fewer Apr 12, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida

item.title: World Series: Season's-best Brewers, Rays tangle for first MLB crown
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt takes a throw as he practices his pickoff during team workouts for the World Series on Thursday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI MIAMI, Oct. 23 (UPI) -- MLB's best two teams will fight for their first World Series title starting Friday when the Milwaukee Brewers host the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 1. The first pitch of the 2026 Fall Classic is scheduled for 8 p.m. EDT at American Family Field. The matchup will be the first World Series game held in Milwaukee since 1982. Each game of the best-of-seven game series will air at 8 p.m. on Fox. "I respect the hell out of them," Brewers manager Pat Murphy told reporters Thursday, when asked about the Rays. "They've done an incredible jobs of winning baseball games." The least-expensive ticket price for Game 1 was $2,154 on the secondary market as of Thursday morning. The least-expensive ticket for Game 3, the first game in St. Petersburg, Fla., was $764. "I've been incredibly impressed with the way our entire roster has handled the intensity of all of these games we've played," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "I know they're excited and they'll be pretty amped up and [Friday] will probably be really, really loud in the other team's favor. Tampa Bay Rays players warm up during team workouts for the World Series on Thursday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI "But we'll take that all in and know we are going to return the favor when we get back to the Trop for Game 3." The Brewers, who posted an MLB-best and franchise-record 103-59 regular-season mark, are favored in the series. Oddsmakers expect the title series to go six games. Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski warms up during team workouts for the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI But the Rays, who last hosted a World Series game in 2008, most likely won't go quietly. They finished their 2026 campaign with an American League-best 98-64 record. They tied the Brewers for the best batting average (.258) in baseball and boast one of the speediest squads in the game. The Rays, who struck out an MLB-low 1,145 times this season, led the American League in stolen bases with 164, just two more than the Brewers' total. The Rays trailed only the Brewers in total hits -- 1,422 to 1,405. Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Nick Martinez throws a ball during team workouts for the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI From a pitching standpoint, the Brewers also were among the best in the game. They led the National League with 3.51 ERA. Their .221 batting average against and 1,186 hits allowed were the second-best marks in MLB. The Rays' pitching staff ranked fourth in batting average against (.229) and hits allowed (1,235). Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI "But we'll take that all in and know we are going to return the favor when we get back to the Trop for Game 3." The Brewers, who posted an MLB-best and franchise-record 103-59 regular-season mark, are favored in the series. Oddsmakers expect the title series to go six games. Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski warms up during team workouts for the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays on Thursday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI But the Rays, who last hosted a World Series game in 2008, most likely won't go quietly. They finished their 2026 campaign with an American League-best 98-64 record. They tied the Brewers for the best batting average (.258) in baseball and boast one of the speediest squads in the game. The Rays, who struck out an MLB-low 1,145 times this season, led the American League in stolen bases with 164, just two more than the Brewers' total. The Rays trailed only the Brewers in total hits -- 1,422 to 1,405. Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Nick Martinez throws a ball during team workouts for the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Thursday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI From a pitching standpoint, the Brewers also were among the best in the game. They led the National League with 3.51 ERA. Their .221 batting average against and 1,186 hits allowed were the second-best marks in MLB. The Rays' pitching staff ranked fourth in batting average against (.229) and hits allowed (1,235). Milwaukee Brewers left fielder Jackson Chourio laughs during team workouts for the World Series on Thursday at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Photo by Tannen Maury/UPI This postseason, the Brewers led MLB with 10 home runs and hit a league-best .250. The Rays ranked third with a .232 average and seven homers. "They've got similar talent," Murphy said. "They try to beat you in different ways, which is similar." Designated hitter Yandy Diaz, first baseman Jonathan Aranada, third baseman Junior Caminero, catcher Liam Hicks, second baseman Richie Palacios and outfielder Chandler Simpson have been among the Rays' playoffs heroes at the plate. They recorded at least four RBIs apiece this postseason. Left fielder Jackson Chourio, center fielder Garrett Mitchell, first baseman Jake Bauers and catcher William Contreras were among the offensive stars for the Brewers during their run to the World Series. Contreras' three playoff homers are tied for the second-most in MLB. Chourio and Mitchell also swatted two homers apiece this postseason. Bauers' six RBIs trail only Chourio's seven for the most among Brewers sluggers. Second baseman Brice Turang, who recorded a .563 on-base percentage en route to NLCS MVP honors, is among other Brewers to watch. Pitching-wise, the Brewers will turn to ace flamethrower Jacob Misiorowski, who eclipsed 105 mph with his fastball this season, in Game 1. He led MLB with a 1.80 ERA this season and logged a 3.24 mark this postseason. "It's an honor to be in this situation and try to propel the team to win," Misiorowski said. The Rays, who were led by Cy Young candidate Drew Rasmussen this season, will start Nick Martinez in the World Series opener. "It's exciting," Martinez said. "As a team, as a staff, we are confident in whoever we call up to the mound. It fell on me. My job is to rack up as many outs as we can and keep us in this ballgame." Murphy will manage at his first World Series, while manager Kevin Cash takes the Rays to the title series for a second time. His Rays lost to the Los Angeles Dodgers in six games in the 2020 title series, which featured fan attendance limitations and a neutral field due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Cash expects a home-field advantage to aid the Rays' effort this time around. "2020 was as special as any season I've been a part of," Cash said last week after the Rays won the ALCS. "But saying that, we didn't have 40,000 people behind us. Excited to see what those 40,000 people bring in Games 3, 4 and 5." World Series schedule All times EDT Friday Game 1: Rays at Brewers at 8 p.m. on Fox Saturday Game 2: Rays at Brewers at 8 p.m. on Fox Monday Game 3: Brewers at Rays at 8 p.m. on Fox Tuesday Game 4: Brewers at Rays at 8 p.m. on Fox Wednesday Game 5 (if necessary): Brewers at Rays at 8 p.m. on Fox Oct. 30 Game 6 (if necessary): Rays at Brewers at 8 p.m. on Fox Oct. 31 Game 7 (if necessary): Rays at Brewers at 8 p.m. on Fox

item.title: Carrick faces media as pressure mounts; Hürzeler has ‘no time’ for rumours; Dortmund fight the influencers: football – live
item.description: ⚽ All the latest news going into the weekend’s action ⚽ Premier League: weekend guide | Mail Tom Álvaro Arbeloa’s been talking ahead of Fulham’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, and buoyed up by last weekend’s much needed win over Hull. “Nothing has changed for us,” insisted the manager, “we were not winning games but we believed in ourselves, we were doing so many things well, “The most important thing [about the Hull win] is we were in same situation against Manchester United and Ipswich but didn’t win but now we had to improve in our transition and did. We controlled the ball in their half better than before.” As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Sunday’s match at Camp Nou will be watched by hundreds of millions of viewers all over the world. A clásico always carries significance, but this weekend’s edition will be especially significant. A Barça win would move them nine points clear of their rivals at the top of La Liga . A Real Madrid victory could be a catalyst for the rest of their season. Continue reading...

item.title: Max Verstappen weighs up first engine penalty of 2026 F1 season
item.description: Max Verstappen cannot rule out taking an engine penalty at some stage during the closing rounds of the 2026 F1 season. Three rounds prior to this weekend's US GP in Austin, Verstappen took new power unit components after issues in Baku Qualifying, but warned a future grid penalty was inevitable. Since the Azerbaijan GP, Verstappen has been in scintillating form, haven taken two consecutive victories at the following Grands Prix in Malaysia and Singapore. The Dutchman now sits P4 in the Drivers' standings, just eight points behind long-time rival Lewis Hamilton, while Red Bull sit just seven points behind McLaren in third in the Constructors'. So far this season, Verstappen has avoided any power-unit related penalties, but his Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar has not been so fortunate. The Frenchman saw a five-place grid drop in Malaysia followed up with a start at the back of the grid in Singapore over turbocharger, exhaust, ICE and PU-ANC changes beyond the allocated limits. During Hadjar's three-race absence due to a wrist injury, stand-in Liam Lawson started at the back of the grid at Monza, which in fact dipped into Hadjar's allocation. Verstappen addresses engine penalty fears Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen, meanwhile, is right on the edge of his power unit limits. The four-time world champion is on his final set of the ICE, turbocharger, MGU-K, energy store, control electronics, and the exhaust systems. The Dutchman has also used five of his six PU-ANC parts. Speaking on Thursday, Verstappen addressed the possibility of an engine penalty at some stage in the coming rounds, but could not pinpoint when exactly it would be incurred. Verstappen said: "We have to take a penalty at one point? Yeah, potentially. But there's no known date to that at the moment. So we just see what happens." Verstappen reveals spine damage in 'unacceptable' outburst on bumpy F1 tracks Elsewhere, Verstappen heavily criticised the track surface at COTA, and revealed some spinal damage he believes he has suffered as a result of years' worth of driving at bumpy circuits. He said: "Last year, for example, you pull around 5-6G in a corner, but I had some impacts, vertical load, which was over 9G on my spine, which I can tell you is really not fun, and especially the older you get, you think about that more and more."

item.title: Stepping out of brother's shadows, this Idaho QB set the state TD record
item.description: Titus Vidlak fondly remembers roaming the sidelines of Hidden Valley High School (Grants Pass, OR) while his father, Mark, coached his elder brothers, Sam and Nate. He was always looking to soak up the moments while his brothers played. But little did he understand then the enormous shadow his elder brothers cast, both with historic prep careers and Division I collegiate careers. So how does the second-youngest Vidlak respond to sitting in the shadows of his elder brothers? By breaking the Idaho career touchdown record during his senior season, of course. "I always kind of wanted to be one of the people on the big field when I was little," Titus told USA TODAY Sports. "So, I definitely looked up to them and now it's my turn. It's pretty exciting, always kind of watching your older brothers do cool stuff and then it's finally your turn, you get to go play." Titus and the Fruitland Grizzlies (5-3) take on Cole Valley Christian (Meridian, ID) on Friday, Oct. 23, in the regular season finale and Titus' senior night. Sam and Nate set the standard for Titus Vidlak Both Sam and Nate were all-state players in high school in Oregon. Sam won Oregon Class 3A Player of the Year in football in 2019 after leading Hidden Valley to its first state championship game in 41 years. He was also a baseball standout. Nate was a dominant pitcher and quarterback , winning the 2021 Oregon Class 4A Player of the Year in baseball after leading the Mustangs to their first-ever state title in baseball. With Sam playing quarterback and Nate at receiver, the duo led Hidden Valley to the Class 3A state championship game in 2019, where Sam threw for an OSAA state championship game-record 479 yards. Mark served as the Hidden Valley offensive coordinator and the head baseball coach. Sam went on to a collegiate career spanning Oregon State, Boise State, Montana and Stephen F. Austin, while Nate elected to attend College of Idaho for both baseball and football, foregoing a baseball scholarship at Oregon. "It's definitely impacted me in a way where I've definitely looked up to them a lot," Titus said. "They, along with my dad, have been my coaches throughout my career. I was always kind of around them. They always work really hard. So I would say whenever they go to the field, I just tag along and be the snapper or catcher, do whatever I can." Following Nate's graduation in 2022, the family moved to Idaho. “(We) wanted a better life and a chance to see Sam at Boise State and Nate at College of Idaho," Mark told USA TODAY Sports. He was always looking to soak up the moments while his brothers played. But little did he understand then the enormous shadow his elder brothers cast, both with historic prep careers and Division I collegiate careers. So how does the second-youngest Vidlak respond to sitting in the shadows of his elder brothers? By breaking the Idaho career touchdown record during his senior season, of course. "I always kind of wanted to be one of the people on the big field when I was little," Titus told USA TODAY Sports. "So, I definitely looked up to them and now it's my turn. It's pretty exciting, always kind of watching your older brothers do cool stuff and then it's finally your turn, you get to go play." Titus and the Fruitland Grizzlies (5-3) take on Cole Valley Christian (Meridian, ID) on Friday, Oct. 23, in the regular season finale and Titus' senior night. Sam and Nate set the standard for Titus Vidlak Both Sam and Nate were all-state players in high school in Oregon. Sam won Oregon Class 3A Player of the Year in football in 2019 after leading Hidden Valley to its first state championship game in 41 years. He was also a baseball standout. Nate was a dominant pitcher and quarterback , winning the 2021 Oregon Class 4A Player of the Year in baseball after leading the Mustangs to their first-ever state title in baseball. With Sam playing quarterback and Nate at receiver, the duo led Hidden Valley to the Class 3A state championship game in 2019, where Sam threw for an OSAA state championship game-record 479 yards. Mark served as the Hidden Valley offensive coordinator and the head baseball coach. Sam went on to a collegiate career spanning Oregon State, Boise State, Montana and Stephen F. Austin, while Nate elected to attend College of Idaho for both baseball and football, foregoing a baseball scholarship at Oregon. "It's definitely impacted me in a way where I've definitely looked up to them a lot," Titus said. "They, along with my dad, have been my coaches throughout my career. I was always kind of around them. They always work really hard. So I would say whenever they go to the field, I just tag along and be the snapper or catcher, do whatever I can." Following Nate's graduation in 2022, the family moved to Idaho. “(We) wanted a better life and a chance to see Sam at Boise State and Nate at College of Idaho," Mark told USA TODAY Sports. Titus Vidlak conducts a record-breaking career Titus has more than lived up to the legacies that his brothers put together in their prep careers as a two-time conference offensive player of the year and the 4A All-Idaho Player of the Year as a junior. He has scored 113 touchdowns entering play on Friday, Oct. 23. Titus broke the record previously set by Keegan Duncan (106), who went on to play linebacker at Utah State and win Idaho's Gatorade Player of the Year in 2018. He broke Duncan's 2018 record on Sept. 18 in a 41–13 road win over Bonners Ferry (ID). That night Titus scored six total touchdowns (three passing and three rushing) to go along with 297 passing yards and 98 rushing yards. "I didn't know I was in the running for it and I didn't really know they kept track of it," Titus said with a laugh. Before that game, Titus had no knowledge that he was close to breaking any record. Neither did Sam. Mark kept everyone in the dark. That was until wide receivers coach Matt Frye informed the team following the game about Titus' record-breaking performance. "In the locker room after the game, our receivers coach gave an awesome speech and surprised me with a plaque and a cool shirt, so I was excited about that," Titus said. "So I was really surprised, but I was definitely super excited and thankful." "I was definitely blindsided by it as well," Sam added. Now, Titus is on the cusp of more Idaho state history. Entering play on Friday, he has 9,149 career yards. That trails Tanner Magnum (Eagle High School) by 450 yards (9,599) for the most career yardage in Idaho history. Titus will have one more regular season game and at least one playoff game to break the record. Sam Vidlak serving as offensive coordinator In his collegiate career, Sam finished with 5,733 career passing yards, 57 touchdowns and 15 interceptions across five seasons with Oregon State, Boise State, Montana, and Stephen F. Austin. He threw for 5,073 yards, 49 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2024 and 2025. After his collegiate career, Sam said he wanted to coach in some capacity at the high school level. He took the role of offensive coordinator and coached his brother in his senior season, joining his father's coaching staff. Mark is in his final year as a high school coach, a role he began in 1998. "When I knew I was going to be around here, I definitely knew I wanted to coach and then I was just wanting to help any way I could," Sam said. "To me, it was less about the role and more about getting to invest in Titus and all his teammates and make some special memories coaching with my dad and getting to coach Titus." "I am probably the first guy ever to walk into the all-time touchdown record holder my first year as an offensive coordinator," Sam added with a laugh. Titus has been a four-year starter for Fruitland. He had 617 passing yards as a 14-year-old during his freshman season. As a sophomore, he threw 2,642 all-purpose yards and 33 touchdowns. In his junior season, Titus finished with 2,720 yards passing, 32 touchdowns and two interceptions, while adding 880 rushing yards and 14 more scores to earn Idaho Statesman's 4A All-Idaho Player of the Year. Titus has continued to improve, completing 73-of-103 passes for six touchdowns and two interceptions, while adding 81 rushes for 829 yards and 16 rushing touchdowns in his senior season. This despite missing one game with mononucleosis and losing another due to an opponent forfeit. He's soaking in every moment to learn from his brother, too. "It's been really special for sure, Titus said. "Sam definitely has a lot of knowledge and knows what it's like to be a quarterback. He's really detailed and it's just really fun." From Idaho to Montana State After a historic prep career, Titus will follow in his elder brother's footsteps and head to Division I football. 247Sports Composite Rankings rank him as a three-star QB in the 2027 class, and he has been committed to Montana State since Dec. 21, 2025. While he is committed to Montana State, Titus also holds offers from Stephen F. Austin, Sacramento State, and most recently, New Mexico. However, the Bobcats were the first team to really recruit him, and that helped him stay committed. "They believed in me early, before really any schools were talking to me about potentially going there," Titus said. "The coaching staff there is amazing. They just came off an (FCS) National Championship, have great coaches and a scheme that fits me well." Sam admitted he attempted to get his younger brother to follow in his footsteps by attending Stephen F. Austin, where Nate also ended his collegiate baseball career in 2025. By committing to Montana State, Titus is ready to make his own collegiate path. "(Stephen F. Austin) was my first offer," Titus said. "(Sam) definitely guided me for a lot of the recruiting, but never really told me exactly where to go. Titus said having time to watch both his elder brothers play the position before him, he's picked parts of their game to add to his own. "They both have parts of their game that I've definitely tried to model," Titus said. "Sam throws it like nobody I've ever seen, and Nate throws it on the run like nobody I've ever seen. So they are both definitely just studs, so it's good." This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Stepping out of brother's shadows, this Idaho QB set the state TD record

item.title: Former Maryland coach Mike Locksley eyeing move to TV commentary, possibly with BTN
item.description: Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images Mike Locksley is about to get paid a lot of money to stay home and do nothing, but the longtime college football coach doesn’t plan to sit around. Locksley and the university parted ways on Wednesday after Maryland dropped to 2-5 following a home loss to fellow Big Ten basement-dweller Rutgers. He finished with a 38-49 record over eight seasons, reached three consecutive bowl games, and posted eight-win seasons between 2021 and 2023, but he also had four losing seasons, and the Terps finished 16-47 in Big Ten play during his tenure. Locksley, who served as an assistant under Nick Saban before taking the Maryland job, spoke with ESPN’s Heather Dinich about his situation , saying that while he thinks his head-coaching career is over, he is considering assistant roles in the NFL or a high-level college program. He also added that, in the interim, he plans to do TV commentary work, “possibly with the Big Ten Network.” Locksley has been a mainstay on college football sidelines since 1992, so he has no history in a dedicated media role. Dinich added that he wants to try it to “get some practice in and see how much he enjoys it.” Whatever he does, Locksley benefits from being paid double. He was set to earn $6.4 million this year and is owed a $9.75 million buyout, per ESPN’s Pete Thamel. The deal has no offset or mitigation, meaning Maryland will pay it all even if Locksley lands another job, Dinich said. The post Former Maryland coach Mike Locksley eyeing move to TV commentary, possibly with BTN appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Rumor Confirms Bloodline vs. 946 in Survivor Series: War Games: Guessing The 5th & Final Member For Both Teams
item.description: WWE One of the hottest stories on WWE Raw over the last month has been the intensifying war between the Bloodline and 946. For weeks, the new faction has been getting the better of the legendary group. However, on this week’s edition of Raw, the rivalry intensified as World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns got involved for the first time. The assumption of many is that the battle will continue into next month and culminate in a cataclysmic clash at Survivor Series in War Games. That expectation was confirmed in a new report from Wrestle Votes on Thursday. Furthermore, the industry insider added that the plan is for the bout to be a classic five-on-five matchup. That means both sides need to add one more person to their side before Survivor Series. With that in mind, we offer up guesses for who could join the Bloodline and 946 for War Games. 946: Dion Lennox Dark State slowly seems to be dissolving as a faction, and that is for the best. While the group has been underwhelming, one of the few bright spots is that it has showcased the upside of NXT talent, Dion Lennox. The former college football and NFL talent is a very good athlete, but what makes him a nice fit for 946 is his believable intensity. Bloodline: Jacob Fatu The likely fifth member for The Bloodline will probably be a returning Jacob Fatu. The “Samoan Werewolf” was hit by a speeding car driven by Jaida Parker last month on the night she revealed she had joined 946. The former United States Champion has been sidelined ever since. However, making a triumphant return to join his family for War Games would deliver some highly entertaining television. 946: Saquon Shugars In terms of performers already on the roster that would be a good fit for 946, NXT’s Saquon Shugars also makes sense. He is a rock-solid wrestler with a street edge that matches the approach of 946. Furthermore, having a bump machine that brings some comic relief is useful for a faction, and Shugars could bring that. Bloodline or 946: Sami Zayn On this week’s Raw, Reigns wondered aloud about who Sami Zayn is loyal to: The Bloodline or himself. That could be a fun question to answer on the road to Survivor Series. Reuniting with his one-time “family,” as he did in 2024, makes sense. Especially if he ended up betraying them to add another layer to his current heel persona. Zayn could also stab the Bloodline in the back before then and side with 946 as their final member as well. Either way, he is a total wild card before Survivor Series. 946: Omos If WWE wanted to make 946 a monster of a faction that seems unstoppable, adding Omos to the group would certainly do that. Due to his size, the creative department has had trouble finding a place for him on the main roster. So they sent him to AAA, where he has gotten to work with The Undertaker to help develop his character. Bringing him back as a more polished performer and the new muscle of 946 would make the group absolutely terrifying. Bloodline: Zilla Fatu Fans who only watch

Last year, for instance, the New York Jets traded away two defensive stars, defensive lineman Quinnen Williams and cornerback Sauce Gardner, for three total first-round picks. Still, most of the players on our board will not be traded. The fun is in considering all the options. Contracts and the salary cap are important factors in facilitating trades. A team acquiring a player in a trade takes on any unpaid money in that player’s contract. A team trading away a player takes on any already-paid cash as dead money. For each player, we have included a projected 2026 cap hit for the acquiring team. Each figure assumes a trade on deadline day, Nov. 10. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders links Articles Commanders.com NFC East roundup | The division struggled but remains wide open Giants Looking ahead to the Houston Texans: The Texans’ No. 3 run defense won’t do the Giants any favors. Houston is coming off a 34-31 victory against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars in London. It held Jacksonville’s top rusher, former Commander Chris Rodriguz Jr., to 55 yards on 11 carries. The Texans announced Tuesday that Tank Dell will return to action for the first time since Dec. 21, 2024, when he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap against the Kansas City Chiefs. He’ll likely be on a snap count, but the standout receiver will join a room that also now includes Marvin Harrison, Jr., who had three catches for 34 yards in his debut. Cowboys & Eagles The Eagles are riding a four-game losing streak — their longest streak since Doug Peterson’s 4-11-1 season in 2020 and the first in the Nick Sirianni era. Philadelphia will also be without Hurts for the remainder of the season as he recovers from deep blood clots. The Cowboys have dropped back-to-back games following their 23-13 Sunday Night Football loss to the Green Bay Packers. Both Philadelphia and Dallas enter the matchup with the same 2-4 record, so a victory would push the [the winner] to 3-4 overall [record]. Commanders What worked: The Commanders almost rallied back from a 23-3 deficit to upset the unbeaten 49ers in the second half. They fell by just one score, 23-17, and the comeback was a valiant effort from Jayden Daniels leading two touchdown drives and a defense that forced three consecutive three-and-outs. Washington contained San Francisco’s offensive weapons in the second half, namely by bringing Brock Purdy to the ground three times for a total loss of 15 yards and limiting him to just four passes in the final 30 minutes. The defense stepped up in critical moments; Jeremy Reaves recorded an important pass breakup in the secondary that prevented George Kittle from converting on third-and-11, and he also brought Christian McCaffrey down short on a third-and-8. Although they are tied for No. 1 in the NFL in turnover differential at +6, the Commanders still have a point differential of -40. Washington is generating takeaways and putting pressure on offenses, yet the turnovers aren’t solving its problems on offense and generating points to win games. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Defense vs 49ers In the first half, the 49ers offense dominated, scoring touchdowns on three of their first five possessions and were well on their way to another score on the fourth possession before K’Lavon Chaisson punched the ball out and the Commanders got a turnover. In the second half, the 49ers scored a field goal on their first possession and then went three and out on three consecutive drives to end the game. That makes it sound like the Commanders came out with a terrible game plan and then switched at half time and it all worked perfectly. I don’t think that was the case. But there was a noticeable change in approach early on which didn’t work for Washington at all. That change lines up interestingly with the news that the Commanders have hired Steve Wilks to help with game planning on the defensive side of the ball. Wilks apparently started last week prior to the 49ers game and on the opening drives for the 49ers, we saw a big shift in philosophy from the Commanders defense. Under Daronte Jones, the Commanders defense are running their interpretation of Brian Flores’ scheme in Minnesota. It’s an ultra aggressive, blitz heavy scheme. But on the 49ers opening possession, the Commanders went away from that philosophy entirely and played a lot more basic zone coverage with just four man rushes up front. It didn’t work for them… What was new was the continued theme of dropping seven into zone coverage and rushing just four. We’ve seen already this season that the Commanders don’t have the defensive line capable of generating a consistent pass rush with just the front four. So to come into this game with the game plan of rushing four and dropping seven into coverage, rather than persisting with the blitzing style that has been the only form of pressure so far this year, is questionable. Chaisson strip-sacked Jameis Winston against the Giants, then eight days later peanut-punched

item.title: ‘Start another streak’ – Shai Gilgeous-Alexander gets real on subbing out to break his 20-point streak vs. Nuggets
item.description: Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images Two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander hopes that he can start something new after his 20-point streak ended in the OKC Thunder’s 96-84 win vs. the Nuggets. With less than two minutes left, SGA had 17 points and looked like a player who could score more against the Nuggets’ defence. But with Thunder already having secured the win over the Nuggets, both teams started to introduce their benches. Seeing this, the reigning MVP decided to sit out for the rest of the game. This meant that the Canadian was going to let go of his 141-game streak of scoring 20+ points. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander wanted to respect the game The Thunder had a 17-point lead at the time Gilgeous-Alexander subbed himself out of the game. He extended the lead in style by draining a dagger three and celebrated by running around the court taking all the love from the fans. There was a moment when it felt like Shai was going to get back and extend his record, but he decided that his night was over after seeing the Nuggets rotation that was going to come onto the court. “I was gonna go out there. But then I saw that they had subbed, so I was like, ‘I should probably sub too.’ I feel like you should always treat the game with respect and God willing, I’ll have many more games to start another streak, so it’s alright,” said SGA in his press conference. Coach Mark Daigneault was full of praise for the two-time MVP after he decided to sit out despite having a shot at extending his impressive scoring streak. “I just have to note, he asked out of the game at the end and he’s got a historic streak going, which is a remarkable streak, obviously. I just think for the class that he shows and the respect that it shows for him to say, ‘Hey, I am out now; the game’s calling for me to be subbed out,’ That was his substitution… It shows tremendous class as a competitor,” Daigneault said in his presser. It was a great comeback from SGA during the game as he struggled in the first half, scoring just 2 points, which came from free throws. He added five more in the third quarter before having big shots in the final quarter to end up with 17 points on the night. SGA will be hoping to have a better scoring performance when the Thunder play his former team, the LA Clippers, next season. item.title: Lions vs. Packers preview, prediction: On Paper
item.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions plays against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers are in town for a big NFC North matchup. The division is establishing themselves as one of the best in the NFL, so whoever wins this game will make an important statement, while the loser will have a bit of a hole to climb out of with three losses on the year. Which team has the statistical edge? Let’s take a look in our On Paper Lions vs. Packers preview and prediction. Lions pass offense (13th in DVOA) vs. Packers pass defense (2nd) The Lions’ passing attack continues to be one of the more reliable units on the team. Jared Goff has been amazingly consistent throughout his Lions career, producing a top-10 or top-five unit for four years running. Thus far this season, Detroit ranks: Second in passer rating (111.3) Seventh in yards per attempt (7.8) Third in dropback EPA (0.304) Fifth in dropback success rate (50.9%) Aiding Goff’s MVP-like campaign is an offensive line that has come together quicker than expected. The Lions rank fourth in ESPN’s pass block win rate (58%), third in PFF pass blocking grade (73.2), 11th in pressure rate allowed (32.4%), and 13th in sack percentage (5.4%). There has been some issues when it comes to blitzes (time to pressure is third-highest at 2.21), but that hasn’t stopped Goff from being extremely efficient against the blitz (+0.33 EPA/pass, second-best). The only big question with this unit is how the return of starting center Cade Mays will impact the unit. Will he be an immediate upgrade from Juice Scruggs, who played well? Or will there be an acclimation period that will result in some missed assignments? The Packers are the most formidable foe the Lions have faced this year when it comes to defending the pass. Now, it’s important to note that they have faced a few backup quarterbacks this year, including Carson Wentz, Jalon Daniels, Case Keenum, and Tyson Bagent. Still, last week’s performance against the Cowboys was impressive, and shouldn’t be pushed to the side. Thus far, Green Bay ranks: Third in passer rating allowed (73.9) Third in yards per attempt (5.9) Seventh in dropback EPA (-0.024) 14th in dropback success rate (45.5%) That last stat suggests a unit that may be bolstered a bit by big plays. And, indeed, that is at least part of the case. The Packers have successfully created a lot of sacks (15, 12th) and turnovers (nine interceptions, first). That is due to the aggressive nature of this defense. They make up for a mediocre defensive line with a high blitz rate (31.7%, 13th) and disguised coverages thanks to their elite pair of safeties. They rank second in total pressures (100), fourth in pressure rate (41.2%), and ninth in average time to pressure (2.58). They are able to do that despite ranking 30th in pass rush win rate (42%) and 26th in PFF pass rush grade (63.
item.content:encoded: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 27: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions plays against the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field on November 27, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers are in town for a big NFC North matchup. The division is establishing themselves as one of the best in the NFL, so whoever wins this game will make an important statement, while the loser will have a bit of a hole to climb out of with three losses on the year. Which team has the statistical edge? Let’s take a look in our On Paper Lions vs. Packers preview and prediction. Lions pass offense (13th in DVOA) vs. Packers pass defense (2nd) The Lions’ passing attack continues to be one of the more reliable units on the team. Jared Goff has been amazingly consistent throughout his Lions career, producing a top-10 or top-five unit for four years running. Thus far this season, Detroit ranks: Second in passer rating (111.3) Seventh in yards per attempt (7.8) Third in dropback EPA (0.304) Fifth in dropback success rate (50.9%) Aiding Goff’s MVP-like campaign is an offensive line that has come together quicker than expected. The Lions rank fourth in ESPN’s pass block win rate (58%), third in PFF pass blocking grade (73.2), 11th in pressure rate allowed (32.4%), and 13th in sack percentage (5.4%). There has been some issues when it comes to blitzes (time to pressure is third-highest at 2.21), but that hasn’t stopped Goff from being extremely efficient against the blitz (+0.33 EPA/pass, second-best). The only big question with this unit is how the return of starting center Cade Mays will impact the unit. Will he be an immediate upgrade from Juice Scruggs, who played well? Or will there be an acclimation period that will result in some missed assignments? The Packers are the most formidable foe the Lions have faced this year when it comes to defending the pass. Now, it’s important to note that they have faced a few backup quarterbacks this year, including Carson Wentz, Jalon Daniels, Case Keenum, and Tyson Bagent. Still, last week’s performance against the Cowboys was impressive, and shouldn’t be pushed to the side. Thus far, Green Bay ranks: Third in passer rating allowed (73.9) Third in yards per attempt (5.9) Seventh in dropback EPA (-0.024) 14th in dropback success rate (45.5%) That last stat suggests a unit that may be bolstered a bit by big plays. And, indeed, that is at least part of the case. The Packers have successfully created a lot of sacks (15, 12th) and turnovers (nine interceptions, first). That is due to the aggressive nature of this defense. They make up for a mediocre defensive line with a high blitz rate (31.7%, 13th) and disguised coverages thanks to their elite pair of safeties. They rank second in total pressures (100), fourth in pressure rate (41.2%), and ninth in average time to pressure (2.58). They are able to do that despite ranking 30th in pass rush win rate (42%) and 26th in PFF pass rush grade (63.8). So if the Lions can manage the Packers’ aggressive tendencies and avoid negative plays, this is a winnable matchup. Player to watch: Cade Mays. In his first game as a Lion, he may be one of the more critical pieces for the team. His presnap reads are going to be essential to Detroit’s success, but that is something the Lions believe is one of his strengths. Via OC Drew Petzing: There’s a stability factor there. He plays at a high level. He’s big, he’s physical, he’s really smart. The communication piece is a huge part of playing that position. Advantage: Lions +1. This is a pretty dang even matchup, but the reason I’m giving the Lions an edge is because I believe Green Bay feeds off disruption, and Detroit has done a pretty good job avoiding that. Goff has yet to turn the ball over, and while I expect the Packers to get to the Lions quarterback for a few sacks, that shouldn’t be enough to take them completely out of their rhythm. If the Packers are forced to blitz, Goff has proven he can beat that. Lions run offense (2nd) vs. Packers run defense (27th) It’s been very feast or famine for the Lions’ rushing attack, yet most of the statistics actually show this as a near-elite unit despite the inconsistencies. The Lions rank: 12th in yards per carry (4.4) Eighth in rush EPA (-0.033) Fifth in success rate (46.2%) Detroit is still seeking its first true explosive run, with Jahmyr Gibbs’ longest rush of the season being just 22 yards, but it seems like it’s just a matter of time given the underlying success of the unit. Run blocking is among the league’s best, ranking first in PFF grade (78.1), fourth in adjusted line yards, and 20th in run block win rate (72%). However, short-yardage situations have been a problem. The Lions rank just 20th in power success rate (62%) and they’ve been stuffed on 18% of rushes, which ranks 21st. Still, Gibbs has been impressive. His 18 rushes of 10+ yards ranks third in the NFL, despite playing one fewer games than most backs. Okay, so this is where things are going to look a little weird. On the surface, the Packers have been pretty darn good against the run. They’ve held half of their opponents below 90 rushing yards and four of six below 3.5 yards per carry. But they also got completely smashed by the Falcons, and some of their down-to-down consistency is not as good as the raw numbers look. Overall, the Packers rank: 15th in yards per carry allowed (4.0) 27th in rush EPA (-0.042) 25th in success rate (42.5%) How much is that being dragged down by the Falcons game? Not as much as you think. In the three games since playing Atlanta, Green Bay still ranks just 28th in rush EPA and 27th in success rate. If we include the Falcons game, over the last four weeks, the Packers rank 32nd in rush EPA and t-32nd in success rate. In other words, this is much more of a mismatch than it looks like. Player to watch: Javon Bullard. The Packers’ nickel corner/safety is a force in the run game and will have to be accounted for on every play. Not only does he have a 85.3 PFF run defense grade, but he also has three tackles for loss. Advantage: Lions +2. I’m curious to see how involved the Packers’ secondary will be in the run game, because if they devote too many to Jahmyr Gibbs, it could make them vulnerable on the back end. Still, I think this is a pretty clear advantage in Detroit’s favor, but I’m capping the advantage at just two, because the Lions have been inconsistent and the Packers’ “poor” run defense has really only cost them in one game. Packers pass offense (17th) vs. Lions pass defense (25th) It seems like the Packers’ passing attack is in the midst of turning a corner. That corner is finding an offensive line combination that isn’t a complete disaster. Through the first couple of games, the Packers could barely field an offense due to injuries and subpar play along the offensive line. It’s gotten a little better with some shuffling and additions, but the overall season numbers are still very concerning for Green Bay. They rank 25th in pressure rate, 32nd in time to pressure, 27th in pressures allowed, 32nd in pass block win rate, and 32nd in PFF pass blocking grade. Yet, because they have very good weapons and a solid quarterback, their overall stats aren’t as bad as you may think. The Packers rank: 15th in passer rating (91.8) 12th in yards per attempt (7.5) 14th in dropback EPA (0.131) 21st in dropback success rate (42.9%) Now, if you look at just the last three weeks, the Packers offense is clearly improving: Weeks 4-6: Ninth in passer rating (101.8) Seventh in yards per attempt (8.2) Sixth in dropback EPA (0.248) 14th in dropback success rate (47.1%) As we’ve talked about all week, it’s the Packers’ deep ball that is most concerning this week, as Jordan Love airs it out more than any other quarterback in the league. item.title: Slegers and misfiring Arsenal badly need a result in WSL north London derby
item.description: Gunners’ title hopes have seemingly evaporated and their under-pressure manager faces her latest test against Spurs It says much about Arsenal’s predicament that the team who have conceded 12 in two games are not the side whose manager is under most pressure before a north London derby. Tottenham, four points above their neighbours before Saturday’s meeting, may have been humbled in consecutive Women’s Super League matches – but all eyes are on Renée Slegers. Arsenal are winless in five WSL matches for the first time, and the most decorated club in English women’s football desperately need a turning point. Their failure to beat Birmingham City at home last Saturday, dropping points against a promoted side for the second time this season, again demonstrated the team’s inability to convert possession into goals. They increasingly look like a team stuck in Groundhog Day. Continue reading...

item.title: Pascal Gross: the obsessive runner keeping Brighton ‘one step ahead’ after fast start

Having been part of the Germany squad eliminated in the quarter-finals of Euro 2024 , the midfielder entered – and won – a running race. Gross completed the 8.4km course on Juist, in the East Frisian islands, in 31 minutes and 35 seconds. He is not known as someone who courts attention, and his victory by more than a minute came to light only when a video was posted on social media by a competitor. Continue reading...

item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Europa League: Celtic lose to Celta after leading, Mateta returns in Palace draw
item.description: Sunderland drop points in 1-1 draw but stay unbeaten VAR rules out Juventus winner in draw with Rennes Celtic suffered more Europa League pain as Spanish side Celta Vigo came from behind to win 2-1 at Parkhead. After defeats by Ferencvaros and Benfica in their first two league phase fixtures, Martin O’Neill’s side struggled to impose themselves on the visitors who were neat and tidy without really testing Hoops keeper Sam Johnstone. Germany midfielder Mika Baur fired the home side in front just over a minute into the second half to thrill the Celtic fans but Spain defender Javi Rodríguez scored twice in three minutes – a header then an unstoppable drive – to stun the home side who could not find a way back. Continue reading...

item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Next in line? Main contenders for the Manchester United hot seat
item.description: With Michael Carrick’s future at Old Trafford a matter of some debate, we examine the credentials of those who could succeed him The German was of interest to Manchester City while Omar Berrada was part of the hierarchy on the other side of town. He is highly thought of and would come with an impressive CV for a 39-year-old, having taken charge of Bayern Munich and Germany. Nagelsmann is regarded as an innovator who is very demanding of his players and builds teams to press relentlessly, a concept not currently used at United, as Bruno Fernandes will testify . His spell with Germany was underwhelming, concluding with a 2026 World Cup last-32 defeat by Paraguay , and at Bayern – with an exceptional squad – he won the Bundesliga in his only full season and was sacked the following March with the team second and still in the Champions League. item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
item.description: Bruno Fernandes followed Lisandro Martínez in revolt after his team’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago. And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie. Continue reading...

item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
